name: Innr SP 240 (EU)

radios.note: Zigbee 3.0 on 2.4 GHz; no Wi-Fi. Innr's EU declaration calls it a Zigbee 3.0 smart plug.

matter.note: Zigbee-only plug; Innr's pages found don't mention Matter for it and no CSA listing was found.

apple_home.note: Innr's EU product page states the plug does not work with Apple HomeKit.

google_home.note: No Innr source found that lists Google Home for this plug; only a retailer listing mentions Google Assistant.

alexa.via: Echo with built-in Zigbee hub or Hue Bridge
alexa.note: Innr says it pairs directly with Echo speakers that have a built-in Zigbee hub; other Alexa devices need a bridge such as Philips Hue.

smartthings.note: Innr lists Samsung SmartThings as a compatible Zigbee hub, including power readings.

home_assistant.note: Innr names Home Assistant among systems that show its power readings and says its products work with ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT. Zigbee2MQTT lists the SP 240 with power, voltage, current and energy.

hubRequired.note: Zigbee plug: needs a Zigbee hub such as a Hue Bridge, SmartThings, an Echo with a Zigbee hub or the Innr bridge.

localControl.note: No Innr statement on control without internet found.

energyMonitoring.note: Innr's EU declaration calls it a Zigbee 3.0 smart plug with power metering. Innr says Philips Hue doesn't show the readings; SmartThings, Hubitat, the Innr bridge and Home Assistant do.

maxLoadWatts.note: Innr's product page gives a maximum load current of 16 A; no watt figure found on an Innr page.

summary: The Innr SP 240 (EU) is a Zigbee 3.0 smart plug for EU Type F sockets with power metering and a 16 A maximum load current. It needs a Zigbee hub such as a Hue Bridge, SmartThings or an Echo with a built-in Zigbee hub. Innr says it does not work with Apple HomeKit.
caveats: Needs a Zigbee hub; there is no Wi-Fi.
Philips Hue can switch it but doesn't show its energy readings.
